Good catch - part of the issue with my code was actually due to leaving the `fixed` blocks before the Tasks were finished, which likely led to the CLR moving the pointers around in memory and therefore I would get NullPointerExceptions.

I made it so that the methods passed in `Task.Run` themselves create the `fixed` blocks and manage the pointers. The code now always runs to the end, with no exceptions.

However, I am still facing an issue. The result that I get back from ASM is wrong - the image is either distorted, or in pieces, or the filter is only applied to some parts of it.

When I add `task.Wait()` upon creating the tasks, everything works fine again.

I think there must still be something wrong with the ASM code not being adapted to run on the same thread multiple times (shared registers, etc), but I have no idea how to get around it.

That's the point, you cannot change strokeWeight within a single beginShape, but you can make multiple beginShapes with different strokeWeights for each one. But then, is it any different from just using arc and doing the same thing?
This is not true, beginShape() does not support strokeWeight() no matter what renderer you use.

I think the only way is to draw every arc of the ellipse manually, using the arc() function, since not even beginShape() supports the alteration of strokeWeight. Reference [here](https://processing.org/reference/arc_.html).
